method: Independent image-only reading of the assigned source, anonymous boxes, permitted standing rules/helper, manifest and one prepared set of crops. The source was inspected once for layout and every crop once. No witnesses, first TSV, approved page, report, prior notes, canonical review or comparison was opened. Larger overlapping boxes were read from their own ink and kept consistent with the smaller passages.

box_notes.evidence: The upper number has a separate top stroke and lower curved bowl for 5, followed by a large oval 0 with a small opening on its upper-left side.
box_notes.scope: The complete upper handwritten number is 50.

box_notes.evidence: Two opening quote strokes and two closing quote strokes surround admissible. The word has the d ascender, dotted i forms, two s curves, b/l stems and final e. The following punctuation is densely retraced with several overlapping loops and a separate low dark point. It is tentatively a live question mark, but cancellation of an underlying question mark cannot be ruled out. A separate comma follows. At the right there is a dotted i, a separate e and a terminal stop; no independent stop between i and e is visible.
box_notes.scope: The short form is kept literally as i e.; no missing stop is supplied. The state of the retraced punctuation is explicit.

box_notes.evidence: The q loop and descender, low u/e, two tall l strokes and final e/s return read quelles. One independent underline begins beneath the middle of the word and extends past its final stroke.
box_notes.scope: The underline is associated with the word; its actual stroke begins near the first e, rather than beneath the q.

box_notes.evidence: Si has its dotted i; on is a low joined pair. Vise has an initial v-like low stroke, separate i dot and low s/e ending. La has a tall loop followed by a small a. Courbe has c/o/u/r and a tall b stem, whose very top meets the crop edge, followed by e.
box_notes.scope: All five principal words are included. No final punctuation is visible.

box_notes.evidence: The first word has a broad q-like opening curve, a short descending stem and low u/i with a dot. Existent has x crossing, i dot, s, two tall t forms and low e/n. An exclamation mark is followed by a closing parenthesis and a separate question mark.
box_notes.scope: No independent opening parenthesis is distinguishable before qui, so none is supplied merely to balance the closing one.

box_notes.evidence: After rotation, the first line reads mais il y a. The next line begins with a tall crossed t, a descending j-like stroke, a possible short r and a final s, giving tjrs or tjs; the following une is legible. The long third-line word has a/r/i, tall t/h, low m/e, a second t and isation-like ending. No separate acute over its first e is secure. Two raised quote-like strokes follow at the right, but their attachment to the note rather than adjacent body text is uncertain. The last line reads de, pi, and an innocent-e/s-like word followed by an exclamation mark.
box_notes.scope: The marginal note alone is transcribed, retaining four physical lines. B006 was rotated minus 32 degrees from the source layout. There is no supplied opening quote. The doubtful closing quotes and final singular/plural ending remain explicit. Peripheral body fragments at a different angle, including clipped material near the lower-right edge, are excluded.

box_notes.evidence: The opening and closing parentheses are complete. Inside, the first numeral has two joined bowls and a descending lower return, reading 3; the second is a rounded 0.

At the left q/u is followed by a raised apostrophe, a small low o and an n stroke, giving qu-on. Compose has c/o, a long low m, a p descender, dot-like o and low s/e. The small next group has an a-like point, a short v-like stroke and low e/c join; avec is tentative. Une de, both parentheses, 31 and the following dash are clear. Below the main line the complete added word has two tall f-like stems, e/c/t and i/v/e, read effective.
box_notes.scope: The principal line and the complete visible added word are included. The addition attaches after action in B009. Clipped preceding-line material at the top and incomplete next-line formula material at the bottom are context only.

box_notes.evidence: Donc, une and action are legible. The curved insertion leader starts after action and runs beneath the upper word effective, ending before the live de. The following E has a small k index, then sur, pi and a dash. On the lower line qu- has a distinct apostrophe. The next word has two tall crossed t strokes, a low middle, a d ascender and compact r/e ending, tentatively attendre; the same-page fully visible attendre in B012 supports the ending. D-une, telle, action and the final question mark are legible.
box_notes.scope: The two complete principal lines are included with effective at its observed attachment. The preceding-line fragments along the top are excluded. No extra pronoun or hyphen is added to the question.

box_notes.evidence: Sans has a tall S, low a/n and final s. A heavy rising stroke crosses or retraces the low joins of a/n/s and is continuous with the lower S return. This favors live retracing, but does not securely exclude cancellation. M-y has the low m, separate apostrophe and descending y.
box_notes.scope: Live Sans is preferred while its deletion state remains explicitly doubtful. No separate replacement is invented.

box_notes.evidence: The first word has the two low humps of m and a terminal e return. Voici has v/o, a dotted i, open c and a final dotted i.

The wider view retains the same uncertain state of Sans. M-y attendre has two t stems, low en, d and a visible compact re ending; a separate comma follows. Me voici is clear. A grave accent stands above à; a separate circumflex stands over the first vowel of tâter, followed by un. The next line has peu, la and structure; peu has no independent final r. Two vertically separated dots form the colon. The following l-os has an apostrophe and rounded low o/s. Des is clear. The last word is tentatively variétés, with a tall t and terminal acute-like mark; the earlier accent is not independently secure.
box_notes.scope: Both complete principal lines are transcribed. The lower clipped portions of the following name and punctuation are context only. Neither the word following the colon nor the uncertain accents are expanded or regularized from the surrounding subject matter.

box_notes.evidence: The name has large T, low e/i, c/h, m, the vowel before two tall l strokes, and e/r. Above that vowel there is one short diagonal stroke descending to the right, rather than two separable dots. The grave reading is preferred, with an intended umlaut retained as an alternative. A separate exclamation mark follows.
box_notes.scope: The visible diacritic is not silently changed to a conventional spelling. Very faint outlined traces above the c/h region are not securely identifiable as writing and are not treated as an additional name diacritic or cancellation.

box_notes.evidence: The opening appears to be s/e with a low loop. A separate small low oval is followed by a tall d-like stem and a sequence of low joined arches ending in a short stepped return. Se donner is a tentative reading of those strokes; the dense low middle cannot be fully separated. A clear comma follows.
box_notes.scope: The wording is left doubtful rather than selected from grammar or mathematical context.

box_notes.evidence: The first word has a low rounded e-like stroke, a high curved mark, a t-like stem and low r/e ending, tentatively être. Celle shows c/e, two tall l strokes and e. Ci is separate, with a dotted i. Two distinct vertical dots form the final colon.
box_notes.scope: The substantial blank gap between celle and ci contains no visible hyphen; none is supplied.

box_notes.evidence: Conjecture has the large C, low o/n, descending j, crossed t and ure ending. A distinct hyphen precedes à, whose grave is visible. Further separate hyphens surround tout before hasard. Hasard has its h ascender and terminal d. One continuous underline spans the phrase, and two dots form the colon outside it.
box_notes.scope: The spelling, three hyphens, accent, single underline and colon are retained.

box_notes.evidence: The label a) is complete. U has a lower index with a low initial hook, an arched body and descending right return, reading eta rather than a closed-loop g. The next a has no accent. Bonne has tall b, low o/n/n/e. Réduction has a visible initial accent, d and t stems and dotted i. Sur and the final S are legible. No terminal period follows S.
box_notes.scope: The entire statement is transcribed. Clipped preceding-line material at the top and a separate partial stroke from the following line at the bottom are excluded. A minute spot just before S is not secure intentional punctuation. No mathematical check was performed.

box_notes.evidence: The lower-left foliation has an inclined leading stroke and upright for 1 followed by two closed ovals.
box_notes.scope: The complete lower-left handwritten number is 100; it is recorded as a margin foliation.
